title: 1973 AHSME Problem 22
statement: The set of all real solutions of the inequality \[ |x-1|+|x+2|\lt5 \] is

solutions.text:
For \(-2\le x\le1,\) the sum of the distances from \(x\) to \(-2\) and \(1\) is \(3.\) If \(x\) lies a distance \(u\) outside this interval, the sum is \(3+2u.\) Thus \[ 3+2u\lt5 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u\lt1. \] Extending the interval \([-2,1]\) by \(1\) at each end gives \[ -3\lt x\lt2. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Interpret the two absolute values as the distances from \(x\) to \(1\) and to \(-2\)
Between \(-2\) and \(1\) the sum is constant; outside that interval it increases by twice the distance from the nearer endpoint
